name: Molly Neal
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember skipping rope on a badly tilted playground.” On Sunday, near Studio Boulevard, Molly waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I had a speech ready about service. My old desk mate handed me a skipping rope and counted out loud.
appearance: Molly is easy to recognize by a loose dark braid and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a little coil of soft measuring tape, Molly draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting when listening.
personality: Molly has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Molly's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To play one round with the old skipping rope.
family: Casey King is Molly’s older relative by marriage. Molly sets the time to leave. Casey picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Casey says, “I was furious there was a secret verse until my grandson asked which page of my diary he could read.”
connections: Basil Allard. The remembered seat and the skipping rope give the reunion two different ways of welcoming someone back.

reactions.situation: The person everyone expects to speak wants to sit down
reactions.response: Molly gives the expected speaker a seat and lets the old classmates start talking amongst themselves.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Molly asks the driver to come back on foot and look at the damaged goods before discussing cost.
